question: In September 2025, European Citizens’ Initiative ‘My voice, my choice’ was submitted to the Commission, proposing the creation of a European financial mechanism to support women who want to terminate their pregnancy but are not allowed to do so in their country of residence, by helping them travel to another Member State in which abortion is legal.

According to the EU Treaties, competences in the field of public health and sexual and reproductive rights lie exclusively with Member States (Article 168(7) of the TFEU). The Commission itself has repeatedly reiterated the fact it does not have the jurisdiction to legislate in this area. I therefore ask: 1.

How does the Commission justify considering an initiative that, by proposing a financial fund linked to abortion access, could be interpreted as interfering with national competences and the principle of Member State sovereignty?

In the Commission’s view, could creating an economic mechanism of this kind lead to inequalities or regulatory competition between Member States, compromising legal certainty within the internal market and the EU’s institutional coherence?

What measures will the Commission take to guarantee respect for national legal frameworks and avoid potential conflicts in the cross-border funding of medical practices regulated differently in each country?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.1.2026) The European Citizens’ Initiative ‘My voice my choice’ calls on the Commission to submit a proposal for financial support to Member States that would be able to perform safe termination of pregnancies, in accordance with their domestic law, for anyone in Europe who still lacks access to safe and legal abortion.

The proposed financial support, according to the organisers of the initiative, ‘could take the form of an opt-in mechanism open to Member States on a voluntary basis’. On this basis, the Commission’s registration decision observed that ‘there seems to be no straightforward targeted interference with the competences of Member States to define their own health policy and the organisation of their health services’1.

In accordance with Article 15(2) of Regulation 2019/7882 the Commission will, by 2nd March 2026, set out in a Communication its legal and political conclusions on the initiative, the action it intends to take, if any, and its reasons for taking or not taking action.

Any EU action would need to respect the responsibilities of the Member States for the definition of their health policy and for the organisation and delivery of health services and medical care, which includes the management of health services and medical care, and the allocation of the resources assigned to them (Article 168(7) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union).
1 Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/1158 of 10 April 2024 on the request for registration, pursuant

to Regulation (EU) 2019/788 of the European Parliament and of the Council, of the European citizens’ initiative entitled ‘My Voice, My Choice: For Safe And Accessible Abortion’, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D1158. 2 Regulation (EU) 2019/788 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 April 2019 on the European citizens’ initiative, OJ L 130, 17.5.2019, pp. 55–81.
